name: Urim And Thummim
overview: The Urim and Thummim were sacred objects placed in the breastplate of the high priest, serving as a divine means for discerning God's judgment and guidance for Israel, as seen when Aaron bore them before the LORD (Exodus 28:30; Leviticus 8:8). Only the priests, such as Eleazar, were authorized to interpret the counsel received through the Urim, guiding leaders like Joshua in their decisions (Numbers 27:21). The Israelites sought God's direction through this priestly mediation, especially in times of battle and uncertainty (Judges 1:1; Judges 20:18), underscoring the exclusive priestly role in communicating God's will and the withholding of answers, as in the case of King Saul.
